items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good countdown geography video for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel: the five tiniest countries on Earth. The Narrator is thrilled to be telling you this: enthusiastic, upbeat, bright and very expressive, like an excited friend who can't wait to show you something amazing. Big smile in the voice the whole way. Wide, lively pitch movement: punch each 'Number five', 'Number four'... like a game-show reveal, and make 'And number one: Vatican City.' the biggest reveal of all. Rise with real curiosity on every question, give a tiny comic pause before each punchline ('Game paused.', 'Central Park? 3.4.', 'The entire country.'), and say every number with genuine amazement. The first line 'This whole country is smaller than Central Park.' is a bold, surprising claim. The last line 'Next to that, Monaco looks huge. Even though...' trails off with the voice staying up, mid-thought, so it can loop straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, with short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy or documentary-serious. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same energy level from the first line to the last. Read numbers naturally: '301' as 'three hundred and one', '0.44' as 'zero point four four', '3.4' as 'three point four', '26' as 'twenty-six'. Pronounce 'Tuvalu' as 'too-VAH-loo', 'Nauru' as 'nah-OO-roo', 'San Marino' as 'san muh-REE-no', 'Monaco' as 'MON-uh-ko'.
lines: This whole country is smaller than Central Park.
Here are the 5 tiniest countries on Earth.
Number five: San Marino, trapped inside Italy.
Drop it on New York, and it's about the size of Manhattan.
Yet, the story goes, it's been a republic since the year 301.
Nine islands, and all their land adds up to just 26 square kilometres.
Space is so tight, the airport runway is also the football pitch.
One road circles the entire country.
Drive it once, and you've toured the whole nation in about half an hour.
Yep, the country from the start: 2 square kilometres. Central Park? 3.4.
Out of room, Monaco builds into the sea. Around a quarter of it used to be water.
Just 0.44 square kilometres. About 60 football pitches. The entire country.
Next to that, Monaco looks huge. Even though...
